traceability.notes:
All aspects of story 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS are implemented and verified.
Mapping to Acceptance Criteria: - Core Functionality: The `require-branch-annotation` rule, together with `branch-annotation-helpers`, detects missing @story/@req annotations on all specified significant branch types (if/else, try/catch, switch cases, loops). Jest RuleTester cases cover both positive and negative scenarios across these constructs. - Quality Standards: The rule follows ESLint best practices (RuleModule with meta.schema, messages, and clean visitors) and is decomposed into reusable helpers. Schema-based config plus explicit validation via `validateBranchTypes` handle misconfigurations robustly. - Integration: Tests cover nested ifs, try/catch with separate branches, switches (including default case handling), and multiple loop types. The rule is integrated into the plugin’s dynamic loader and flat-config presets, and is listed in the README. - User Experience: Error messages use `missingAnnotation` with `{{missing}}` to state clearly which annotation (@story or @req) is missing. Tests assert both the messageId and data, and autofix behavior inserts readable placeholder annotations in intuitive positions, including within catch bodies. - Error Handling: Invalid `branchTypes` configurations are turned into ESLint config errors with clear messages. Comment association logic has dedicated tests for tricky CatchClause cases and blank-line switch cases. Nested-branch tests ensure inner branches are enforced independently of outer annotations. - Documentation: A dedicated rule doc (`docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md`) plus README entries document purpose, configuration (including invalid config behavior), and annotated examples, matching the story’s documentation requirements.
Given the passing, targeted tests and aligned documentation and implementation, this story is fully satisfied.
